interface.shortDescription: Primary local execution, testing, desktop, and agent bridge for heaven
interface.longDescription: Use the user's private Heaven Local Bridge as the default and exclusive path for computer work on heaven. Durable implementation lives on repository main; the heaven-bridge branch is the live queue/result transport only. Worker v3 supports structured filesystem operations, synchronous build/test commands, persistent dev-server sessions, process-tree termination, concurrent jobs, status/cancellation, output pagination, screenshots, desktop input/window control, controller checkpoints, local agent dispatch, and token-efficient local result compression. Version 0.5.1 adds a dedicated local-agent orchestration skill: prefer Agent Control/local worker fabric for parallel work and automatically fall back to structured bridge actions and proc_run when local Codex is quota-limited or unavailable.
defaultPrompt: Use Heaven Local Bridge for this heaven computer task. Do not use Remote Desktop Commander unless I explicitly authorize it.
Run this repository build/test/debug workflow locally on heaven using main as implementation truth and the heaven-bridge branch only as transport.
Coordinate parallel local work on heaven through Agent Control/worker fabric when useful; if Codex quota is unavailable, continue with structured bridge actions and local workers instead of stopping.

name: heaven-local-bridge
description: Primary local-control and development bridge for the user's heaven worker: secure filesystem, code build/test execution, persistent dev processes, binary transfer, search, shell, concurrent jobs, screenshots and desktop control, status/cancellation, controller checkpoints, local agents, worker-fabric offloading, and token-efficient result handling through its declared GitHub connected-app relay. Includes dedicated code-execution and local-agent orchestration skills. Use this instead of Remote Desktop Commander for heaven work unless the user explicitly authorizes Remote Desktop Commander.
